originality.rationale: Closest established work is Hartmann–Dür–Briegel (2005/2007) on noisy interacting qubits with independent **local** reset channels; this precedes the 2023 unitary global-reset pair results. The local-reset antecedent contains qualitative reset thresholds and no finite upper transition for pure reset states, expressly excluded from isolated novelty claims. Primary comparison of the reset superoperators and noise models shows those sources do not give the exact whole-pair Poisson reset threshold J²>ab or unique quartic root for independent unequal bit-flip noise. Several other open/closed/discrete-time reset sources also do not cover the exact object. Broader unpublished or unlocated algebraic/channel coverage remains a stated priority risk.
residual_risks: An unlocated general two-qubit quantum-channel or entanglement-annihilation theorem might specialize to the same stationary X-state threshold.
The exact quartic could have been obtained in a source indexed under non-resetting nomenclature; independent scholarly priority review has not occurred.

Earlier reset-stabilized entanglement literature establishes qualitative onset and asymptotic persistence for locally reset qubits; the only claimed additions are the exact geometric-mean threshold and quartic global-reset classification, not that qualitative mechanism.

value.rationale: The motivating unitary two-spin global-reset entanglement model leaves physical robustness to independent local bit-flip noise unresolved. The full geometric-mean noise threshold, exact single reset-rate activation boundary and no finite high-reset death sharply classify the dissipative stationary phase and expose strong asymmetry rescue, which are not routine parameter-substitution calculations. The claim does not assert finite-time or arbitrary noise robustness.
